newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WEEKEND TO REMEMBER FOR MACEDONIA, TURKEY AND NETHERLANDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND TO REMEMBER FOR MACEDONIA, TURKEY AND NETHERLANDS.

text.p: Macedonia, Turkey and the Netherlands scored 25 goals between them on a free-scoring weekend which featured 18 World Cup qualifiers around Europe.

Macedonia's 11-1 win over Liechtenstein on Saturday was the joint-fourth highest victory in the 66-year history of the tournament, bettered only by New Zealand's 13-0 victory over Fiji in 1982, West Germany's 12-0 triumph against Cyprus in 1970 and Mexico's 11-0 rout of St Vincent in 1992.
The Netherlands and Turkey also had matches to remember, with the Dutch hammering Wales 7-1 in Eindhoven and Turkey beating San Marino 7-0 in Ankara.
Group One

Greece, who reached the World Cup finals for the first time in 1994, went top after holding Croatia to a surprise 1-1 draw in Zagreb. Croatia squandered their chance of replacing Denmark at the head of the group, but as they, and the Danes, both have two matches in hand on the Greeks, the result may not prove too damaging for Croatia in the long-term.

Bosnia, fresh from their 2-1 friendly win over Italy last Wednesday beat Slovenia, another former Yugoslav republic, 2-1 to record their first World Cup victory. The defeat was Slovenia's third successive loss and sent them to the bottom of the group.
Group Two

England marked their 100th World Cup match with a well-deserved 2-0 win over Georgia on a bumpy pitch in Tiblisi thanks to first half goals from Teddy Sheringham and Les Ferdinand. It was England's third successive win under new coach Glenn Hoddle and they maintained their 100 percent record to move three points ahead of Italy, their next opponents in February.
Poland gained their first points after their opening 2-1 defeat by England with a 2-1 win over Moldova in Katowice. The results left Moldova bottom without a point from three games.
Group Three

A first-half goal from Oyvind Leonhardsen gave Norway a 1-0 win over Switzerland in Berne which kept Norway top with nine points from three matches and a goal tally of 9-0. Hungary, who beat Azerbaijan 3-0 on Sunday moved above Switzerland into second place with six points from their opening three games.
Group Four

Scotland put behind them last week's arguing in FIFA committee rooms which determined they have to replay their abandoned match against Estonia, to score what could prove to be a priceless 1-0 win over Sweden in Glasgow to go top of the standings. Scotland goalkeeper Jim Leighton marked his 75th international with an outstanding display while John McGinlay's eighth minute goal guaranteed the points. Austria helped complete Sweden's miserable weekend as their 2-1 win over Latvia moved them into second place behind Scotland, level on seven points but with a slightly inferior goal difference. Sweden slipped from first to third.
Group Five

Russia took another confident step towards the finals with a trouble-free 4-0 win over Luxembourg despite playing most of the match with 10-men after having defender Yuri Nikiforov sent off in the first half. They moved three points clear at the top after Israel, who beat Bulgaria and drew with Russia in their opening two matches, surprisingly lost 2-0 to perennial also-rans Cyprus. Before Sunday, Cyprus, whose two goals were both scored by Sinica Gogic inside 15 minutes, had only previously ever won three World Cup matches since first entering the tournament in 1960 -- and two of those were against the Faroe Islands.
Group Six

The only match in the group saw Yugoslavia maintain their 100 percent record with their fourth successive win, a 1-0 victory over the Czech Republic. Real Madrid striker Predrag Mijatovic scored the only goal after 18 minutes. The Czechs remain third but will slip back to fourth if Spain gain at least a draw against second-placed Slovakia when they meet on Wednesday.
Group Seven

Dennis Bergkamp scored a hat-trick as the Netherlands beat Wales 7-1 in Eindhoven which moved the Dutch to the top of the group on goal difference above both Belgium and Wales. The defeat was Wales's heaviest for 66 years and coach Bobby Gould said it was the lowest point in his career. Turkey also hit seven to beat San Marino 7-0, the first time they had scored seven in a match since they beat Pakistan 7-4 in 1967.
Group Eight

Macedonia's 11-1 romp against part-timers Liechtenstein was one of the biggest results in World Cup history and with slightly more luck, Macedonia could have scored 20. They were 9-0 ahead before Liechtenstein replied, and the win moved them top of the group on goal difference above Ireland who were held 0-0 by Iceland in Dublin on Sunday.
Group Nine

The only group in which all six teams were in action over the weekend provided one of the major shock results with Northern Ireland holding European champions Germany 1-1 in Nuremburg. Northern Ireland have now played five games against the Germans over the last 19 years without defeat.
Portugal went a point clear at the top after beating Ukraine 1-0, while Albania were denied only their fifth-ever World Cup win when Armenia equalised in the last minute for a 1-1 draw in Tirana.
